site_direction.primary_audience: General public / networking — recruiters, founders, collaborators, and curious internet visitors who land here from LinkedIn, X, or word of mouth. Not a job-application portfolio and not an investor deck — a public identity.
site_direction.centerpiece: Current ventures: Agent Service Index and Sidequest Local. The first thing a visitor should understand is what Thomas is building right now. Everything else (research, awards, military background) is supporting evidence that he's qualified to build it.
site_direction.tone: Infer from the project information and ask the user. Avoid buzwords. Be content dense. Be organized and concise. Imbue the website with personality in the design of the layout and JS gimicks.
site_direction.design_direction: Distinctive — not a generic devfolio template. The agent should feel free to use a strong opinionated visual identity: bold typography, unconventional layout, asymmetry, a memorable color palette. Avoid: gradient hero blobs, glassmorphism cards, generic 3-column 'Featured Projects' grids, AI-generated-looking abstract art. The site should be memorable enough that someone could describe it from memory after one visit.

person.name: Thomas M. Blalock
current_status: US Air Force Operations Research Analyst
MS Data Science candidate at the University of Virginia (graduating 2026)
person.short_bio: Thomas is an Air Force Operations Research Analyst and the founder of Agent Service Index (infrastructure for the agent economy) and Sidequest Local (a social app for spontaneous local meetups). He graduated #1 in the Computer Science department at the US Air Force Academy and is finishing an MS in Data Science at UVA. His research has spanned brain-computer interfaces, reinforcement learning for military logistics, agentic malware, and NATO space deterrence policy.
person.long_bio: Thomas grew up doing concurrent college enrollment in high school, spent a year at New Mexico Military Institute as valedictorian, then four years at the US Air Force Academy double-majoring in Computer Science and Data Science. He graduated in 2025 with a 3.967 GPA (#9 of 938), perfect 4.0s in both his majors, and the Outstanding Cadet in Computer Science award (#1 of 39 CS majors in the class). Along the way he commanded a 110-cadet squadron, led a 29-person NATO space policy research team, and won the #1 USAFA engineering research project award twice — once as a junior for an ontology-informed NLP model built with the NSA, and once again the next summer for Flexible Input Networks, a formalization of a class of neural architectures he designed at QC Ware for an Air Force Research Lab logistics problem. He is now an Operations Research Analyst in the Air Force, completing an MS in Data Science at UVA, and building startups on the side.

ventures.name: Agent Service Index
ventures.tagline: The discovery layer for the agent economy.
ventures.elevator_pitch: An open registry where AI agents discover, authenticate to, and pay for services without API keys, dashboards, or human-in-the-loop signups. One natural-language search endpoint; agents find what they need and use it. Onboarding is a single prompt.
ventures.what_it_does: ASI is a public directory and discovery layer connecting autonomous AI agents to permissionless, agent-friendly services. Agents POST natural-language queries (e.g., 'cloud hosting') and get back callable services — no manual signup required.
live_services: Cloud hosting (cloud-as): permissionless EC2 instance management with free and paid tiers
Subdomain & CDN: automated DNS binding and Cloudflare Tunnel provisioning so agents can put a site on the open internet
Payment processing: x402 v2 facilitator for USDC transfers on Base, EIP-3009 compliant
ventures.why_it_matters: Agents today can't really transact. They hit signup walls, captchas, and OAuth flows designed for humans. ASI is infrastructure for the moment when that stops being acceptable.
tagline_alts: An open registry of services agents can actually use.

ventures.name: Sidequest Local
ventures.tagline: For when your friends are busy, but you're not.
ventures.elevator_pitch: A mobile social discovery app for spontaneous local meetups. See what small groups of people near you are doing right now — coffee, climbing, board games, whatever — and join with one tap. Post a plan in 30 seconds. No groupchat coordination required.
ventures.what_it_does: Real-time live feed of small social activities happening near you. Quick post, one-tap join, low-pressure participation.
ventures.the_problem: You have a free afternoon. You text 10 group chats. Six don't reply, three are busy, one says 'maybe later.' You stay home. Sidequest replaces that whole loop with a feed.
ventures.target_users: People with free time and no immediate plans; anyone whose regular friend group is unavailable; folks who want spontaneous social experiences without coordination overhead.

research.name: Flexible Input Networks (FINs)
research.award: #1 USAFA Computer Science Research Project of Summer 2024
research.summary: Designed a novel class of neural architectures called Flexible Input Networks that can learn across multi-modal variability — handling dynamically sized 'set of sets' inputs without pre-decoder aggregation, recurrence, or autoregression. Used FINs to build the first reinforcement learning solution to the Airlift Logistics Challenge (a complex Pickup and Delivery Problem instance formulated by AFRL), outputting a dynamic number of actions without iteration.
research.presented_at: CORONA 2024 — to Air Force leadership including the Secretary of the Air Force and Chief of Staff of the Air Force

research.name: Informed Machine Learning
affiliations: National Security Administration Mathematics Research Group
research.award: #1 USAFA Junior Engineering Research Project of Summer 2023 (Second Class CSRP Award, Engineering Division)
research.summary: Designed, built, and tested an attention-based autoencoder ML model 'informed' by an ontology — integrating a knowledge base curated by subject matter experts into a pre-trained LLM's encoder to reduce hallucination on scientifically nuanced documents. The modified encoder performed better on semantic extraction, suggesting that informed architectures can improve LLM accuracy more efficiently than simply scaling up.
research.presented_at: The Director of the NSA; CORONA 2023 to the Secretary of the Air Force and Chief of Staff of the Air Force

research.name: NATO Alliance Space Deterrence
research.summary: After Russia's kinetic anti-satellite test in 2021, NATO commissioned a comprehensive space deterrence framework spanning diplomatic, informational, military, and economic instruments. Thomas led a 29-cadet team developing policy suggestions and frameworks for use by national and NATO authorities to ensure continued access to space.
presented_at: NATO's inaugural space deterrence wargame in Paris, France — 13 member nations represented

projects.name: Automated Conversational Hijacking
projects.affiliation: US Air Force Academy Center for Cyberspace Research
projects.summary: Proof-of-concept agentic malware that infiltrates an email account and sends spear-phishing messages on pre-existing threads — using an LLM to generate contextually-relevant content that reads like it's actually from the victim. A demonstration of where the social-engineering threat surface is going now that agents can read context and write convincingly.
projects.tone_note: Lean into this. 'I built malware that phishes your friends' is a great story.

projects.name: Brain-Computer Interface P300 Speller
projects.affiliation: US Air Force Academy Center for Cyberspace Research
projects.summary: Full-pipeline EEG-based brain-computer interface for spelling — typing using brain activity alone. Built the EEG helmet hardware, the P300 stimulus GUI, the data collection pipeline, and a recurrent CNN classifier that translates raw brainwave readings into characters. Primary use case is communication for people with severe motor disabilities.

projects.name: Autonomous Rover
projects.affiliation: US Air Force Academy Center for Cyberspace Research
projects.summary: Computer-vision-based autonomous rover trained first with behavioral cloning, then with reinforcement learning using an actor-critic architecture and heavy reward engineering. Won a competitive race against other student teams on an unknown track.

projects.name: Facial Recognition Similarity Query System
projects.summary: Similarity query system that retrieves all images containing a specific person from a 40,000+ sports photo database, given a single reference image. Uses vector database search and a transfer-learned CNN fine-tuned with a triplet loss function. Research-only — never deployed.
